name: App Store privacy nutrition labels
plain: A label on each App Store page that lists what data the app collects and whether it is linked to you or used to track you.
meaning: Declared by the developer in App Store Connect with no technical check, so accuracy depends on honesty. Labels went live 14 December 2020.

android.note: Play's equivalent is the Data safety section.

ios.store_policy: Required for all new apps and updates; categories: Contact Info, Health, Financial, Location, and others; Data Used to Track You, Linked, Not Linked
ios.api_surface: App Store Connect > App Privacy; Privacy Nutrition Label
ios.note: Mismatches between label and behavior have drawn rejections and press studies.

limits.headline: Can tell you what the app says it collects, on its App Store page
limits.user_action: You open the app page in the App Store and scroll to App Privacy
can: List data the developer says is linked to you, or used to track you
Show data types such as location, contacts and purchases
Show a label even before you download
cannot: Be checked by Apple with a technical test; the developer fills it in
Prove the claims are true; mismatches have led to rejections and press studies
Appear on Android; Google Play has the Data safety section instead
limits.reach_label: A label, filled in by the developer
limits.differs: Apple privacy labels came out on 14 December 2020. Google Play uses the Data safety section.

story.what_it_is: A nutrition label style box on each App Store page that shows what data an app collects.

marketing.name: App Privacy Details
marketing.pitch: See a summary of the app's privacy practices before you download it.

story.for_you: On the App Store you can read a short list: data used to track you, data linked to you and data not linked. It helps you compare apps.
story.for_makers: Makers fill out the label in App Store Connect. Apple does not check it technically, so honesty is the guard, and press and researchers often test labels against real traffic.

use_cases.example: A social app shows a long list of data linked to you, including contacts and location.
A private messenger shows very little collected, which becomes a selling point.
A free game lists ad data used to track you across apps.
A retailer lists purchases and browsing history as linked to you.
A watchdog compares the label with the SDKs found in the app and flags a mismatch.
A news app uses the label to say it does not track you across other apps.

story.android_note: Android's matching tool is the Data safety section.
